newsitem.title: USA: AOL sets reorganization, new pricing plans.
newsitem.headline: AOL sets reorganization, new pricing plans.

text.p: America Online Inc, responding to challenges posed by the Internet to its leadership as the world's leading provider of online services, introduced on Tuesday a new corporate structure and a set of pricing plans designed to make it more competitive.
AOL said that among the pricing options it would offer was a flat monthly rate of $19.95.

It said it would divide into three operating units: AOL Networks, to oversee the flagship Internet online service; AOL Studios, for creating online programming, and ANS, its network infrastructure arm.
The company said it named Robert Pittman to head AOL Networks.
Pittman is a former chief exectutive of MTV Networks, the cable music network, and more recently the chief executive of Century 21 Real Estate Corpo, to head AOL Networks.
Ted Leonsis, who presently heads AOL Services Co, will lead the newly formed AOL Studios, the company said.
Bruce Bond, hired earlier in 1996 to lead ANS Communications, will continue in his current role, AOL said.

In a statement, AOL chairman Steve Case said that the company had begun to address some of the customer retention problems it encoutered during the summer months, and added nearly 250,000 net new members in October alone.

AOL also said it its new, more competitive pricing structure would begin immediately. The plans calls for two unlimited pricing tiers to provide a "comfort factor" for heavy and medium users, and a $4.95 plan for light users.
AOL said it will charge a standard monthly plan for unlimited AOL use, including Internet access, for $19.95.
It will also offer advance payment rates of $14.95 per month for customers who pay for two years, and $17.95 per month for those who pay in advance for one year.

The company said it will charge a "bring-your-own-access" rate of $9.95 per month, offering unlimited access to the proprietary content only available on AOL to people who already have a separate Internet access connection.
The company said it will offer a light-usage program offering three hours of AOL per month for $4.95, with additional time priced at $2.50 per hour.
In addition, AOL said it will immediately begin expensing all marketing and subscriber acquistion costs as they are incurred, rather than deferring the costs over time as it did previously.
As a result, it said it would take a charge of $385 million as of September 30 to cover subscriber acqusition costs such as the mass mailing of software starter kits.
It also said it planned to take a one-time charge of $75 million in its December quarter to cover the costs of reorganizing the company.

Best known as the broadcast programmer who created MTV, Pittman also headed Time Warner's Six Flags Entertainment amusement park chain, where he oversaw a national brand advertising strategy that resulted in four straight years of record growth in attendance, revenues and earnings, AOL said.
Under Pittman's direction, MTV became the first profitable basic cable network company.
Pittman is a member of the boards of America Online, HFS Inc, 3DO Co, Excite Inc and AMRE Inc and was formerly on the boards of Electronic Arts Inc and MTV Networks.
